title: Local LLM Sim SDK Playbook (sprint notes)
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a compact, reproducible local SDK quickstart that simulates Redwood inference behavior without needing cloud credentialing or a live hosted endpoint. The aim is a 10-15 minute first-run for engineers (product, SRE, solutions) to:
  - run a local mock server that behaves like the Redwood API,
  - exercise the SDKs (Python + TS) end-to-end,
  - validate telemetry events and error paths, and
  - collect minimal performance signals (latency buckets) under a dev load.

Audience:
  - SDK authors and integrators
  - Solutions engineers preparing demos
  - New hires who want a local playground before provisioning Dedicated/Hosted API keys

Non-goals:
  - not a performance benchmark (no GPU, limited load)
  - not a full emulation of rollout policies or routing

Quickstart summary (zero-to-hello in ~10min):
  Prereqs:
    - Node 18+ and Python 3.10+ installed
    - Docker (optional for local server container)
    - git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk (use branch: local-playback)

  1) Start mock Redwood server (two options)
     - Docker (recommended for parity):
         docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/redwood-inference/local-llm-sim:latest
     - Local node: (dev only)
         cd infra/local-llm-sim && npm install && npm run start -- --port 8080
     What it does: exposes /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings, and a /healthz. Returns configurable latency distributions and simple deterministic completions for repeatable tests.

  2) Python SDK quick smoke (examples/python/hello_local.py)
     - virtualenv -p python3 .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
     - pip install -e ./sdk/python -r examples/python/requirements.txt
     - export REDWOOD_API_BASE=http://localhost:8080
     - python examples/python/hello_local.py
     Expected: prints a deterministic completion, a couple of telemetry log lines, and a 200 status. If you see a 401 -> check REDWOOD_API_KEY or set REDWOOD_API_KEY=dev-local-key.

  3) TypeScript SDK quick smoke (examples/ts/hello_local.ts)
     - cd examples/ts && npm ci && export REDWOOD_API_BASE=http://localhost:8080 && node hello_local.js
     Expected: same deterministic completion, plus a small trace JSON written to ./tmp/traces.json

  4) Telemetry contract checks (local only)
     - The mock server accepts telemetry events at /v1/telemetry. Events should contain: client_name, sdk_version, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_id, latency_ms.
     - Run: python tools/check_telemetry.py --source ./tmp/traces.json
     - Failing checks: missing sdk_version or request_id -> mark as blocker for SDK release.

Troubleshooting matrix (common fast fixes):
  - Server 404 on /v1/generate -> ensure REDWOOD_API_BASE set and that container mapped to 8080.
  - Deterministic output different across runs -> remove existing ./tmp/cache.json or run with --seed 42.
  - Slow local responses -> mock server uses latency profile file (infra/local-llm-sim/latencies.yaml). Change to low-latency preset for fast dev loops.
  - Telemetry fails with 429 -> mock server has simple rate limiter: increase window in env or set TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 for the smoke run.

Developer notes & gotchas (lessons learned in sprint):
  - Keep deterministic completions short; long generated sequences make local loops painful. Prefer 8-32 token responses for quick iterates.
  - Example prompts should be explicit: we found ambiguous prompts generate non-deterministic behavior in some open models used in nightly tests.
  - Avoid absolute filepaths in examples; use os.path.join and process.cwd() to keep cross-OS reproducibility.
  - Consider exposing a --fast flag to the mock server that disables artificial latency and rate limits for CI.

Smoke tests & gating checklist (local CI target):
  - [ ] examples/python/hello_local.py runs and returns exit code 0
  - [ ] examples/ts/hello_local.js runs under node 18 and writes trace file
  - [ ] tools/check_telemetry.py reports no missing required fields
  - [ ] lint (python + eslint) passes on examples
  - [ ] minimal integration test: SDK sends a function call simulated payload and mock returns structured JSON; SDK correctly maps it to function call response

Prompt recipes for quick demos (short and citable):
  - "Summarize in one sentence: {{ input }}"  -> deterministic summarization stub
  - "Extract top-3 entities from: {{ input }}" -> returns a JSON array of entities (fixed for demo)

Telemetry & observability checklist (dev-focused):
  - Emit request start and end events with request_id
  - Attach sdk_version and language to all telemetry events
  - Log latency_ms in buckets: <10ms, 10-50ms, 50-200ms, 200-800ms, >800ms
  - Write a small collector in tools/collect_local_telemetry.py that aggregates and prints percentiles for a smoke run

Open questions (to resolve in next sprint):
  - Do we want the mock server to emulate KV cache hits (prefix cache) for a tighter fidelity test? Trade-off: complexity vs value.
  - How much of rollout behavior should be mimicked? Canary failure/fallbacks are useful for platform tests but increase maintenance.
  - Should examples default to using the mock server, or require an explicit flag? I lean explicit (no surprises for new users).

Next steps (action items):
  - Diego: add a --fast CI mode to the mock server and push a new container tag (due 2024-10-15)
  - Anya: write the minimal telemetry assertion script and add to examples CI (due 2024-10-18)
  - Maya: fold the quickstart into the SDK README and create a small video (3-4min) showing the 10-min path (due 2024-10-25)
  - Jordan: run cross-platform smoke on mac/linux/windows runners and capture flaky steps (due 2024-11-01)

Notes to self (quick fragments):
  - "seed" param is the single most useful toggle when debugging non-deterministic generated text.
  - Keep example prompt bank under 200 tokens total so local loops stay fast.
  - Consider a tiny kata: "add a new function call handler" that exercises tool calling and function response mapping.

Unresolved TODOs (parking lot):
  - add an example that demonstrates model fallback (heavy lift)
  - embed a minimal HMAC auth mode for local testing of auth headers
  - document how Dedicated setups differ for telemetry collection

End of sprint note. This doc is intentionally lightweight and iterative; copy into README.md under sdk/examples once we stabilize the smoke checklist.
